why_not_a_blocklist: A list of forbidden words runs to millions and still misses the next one. This profile describes the register instead: his vocabulary sits at a median Zipf frequency of 5.72, and only 2.7% of his words are rare - those being domain terms like agentic, evals and embeddings, or proper nouns. So a word that is neither common English nor already his is off-register without anyone having listed it.
rules: A word absent from both the frozen common-English list and his own corpus is off-register unless it is a proper noun.
Sentence length must vary. Uniform length is the clearest AI signal in his data: his own standard deviation is above 10, while posts he judged AI-sounding sat near 8.
Idioms built from common words - 'shy of' rather than 'short of' - are invisible to frequency and need the judge. The statistical layer is a prior, not a verdict.
The corpus grows with every post he publishes, so false flags shrink over time rather than needing a maintained list.

common_list.source: wordfreq top 12,000 English words, frozen at build time
common_list.sized_by: 12,000 catches 17 of 24 known literary words with zero false flags across his plain and domain vocabulary. 20,000 catches only 12; 30,000 catches 3.
common_list.note: Frozen deliberately. A live frequency dependency would break the zero-runtime-dependency boundary this repository enforces in its hardening tests.
